newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador vice president says social spending needed.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador vice president says social spending needed.

text.p: Ecuador's Vice President Rasoalia Arteaga said that her country must do more to address improve living conditions, and not sacrifice social spending in order to come to agreement with international lenders.

"We have to put forward special bills for social policy because of the poor, and because of problems in health education and employment," Arteaga told Reuters Financial Television on a visit to New York.
She said that Ecuador had developed a good relationshop with the International Monetary Fund over the past few years, but that the relationship had weighed on social programming.
"We have to do more work in social affairs because of the situation of our people," Arteaga said.
She expressed concern that an IMF accord might force Ecuador to decrease its commitment to social spending.
"We have to have a good relations with the (IMF), but one the one hand we have to plan economic things and on the other social affairs."
Arteaga, a frequent critic of President Fabian Alarcon, added that it was too early to determine whether she would remain in politics.
"I have to think well and to decide next month," Artega told Reuters when asked whether she planned on running for president in the election in May 1998.
